constitution_ref: Art. X (one authority, two vocabulary namespaces never mixed), Art. XXV (UNKNOWN is first-class, never fabricated success), Art. LXXXIV (starvation-skip is correct), Art. LXXVII (a mid-chain failure never yields a discovery credit)
method: the REAL EngineRun conductor was driven for every (dependency, case) pair; the consumer behavior was read from the durable stage_log — a MISSING log entry is classified NOT_REACHED, never execution; each case has an explicit expected set and an observed classification, and every (dependency, case, consumer) triple is asserted against its expected set

case_semantics.ok: the dependency executed OK; consumers may execute with typed input or skip
case_semantics.admission: the dependency recorded SKIPPED_ADMISSION (a typed skip, not a failure); consumers may execute against the typed-UNKNOWN input, skip, or never have been scheduled
case_semantics.failed: the dependency recorded FAILED_EXPLICIT; consumers MUST skip or terminate non-discovery, never execute OK
case_semantics.absent: the dependency was never scheduled (the run terminated before its turn); consumers can only skip / not-reach / terminate non-discovery

VERIFY.contract: DECLARED_DEPENDENCY_NOT_RUNTIME_CASCADE: the static depends_on names ['ATTACK', 'ADJUDICATION'], but the conductor's DOWNSTREAM_BLOCKERS does not cascade VERIFY failure to ['ATTACK', 'ADJUDICATION'].  The consumer executes and records its OWN typed state against the (possibly empty) dependency input — a typed UNKNOWN, never a fabricated success (Art. XXV).  This is the CURRENT contract, proven by the case table; it is documented, not refactored.

two_authority_divergence.note: R537 §A: the static declaration and the runtime cascade are TWO authorities.  Where they diverge, the divergence is DOCUMENTED (not a defect to silently fix) — the consumer's typed state against a skipped dependency is the operative contract.  No refactor is performed in R537; the proof + disclosure is the deliverable.
